observations.explanation: The paper defines PS as planning subtasks then carrying them out (pp. 2–3), and distinguishes PS+ by adding variable/numeral extraction and intermediate-calculation instructions (pp. 2–3).

The evaluation covers arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic datasets (pp. 4–6), and reports PS+ gains over zero-shot CoT while not consistently surpassing few-shot CoT—for example, it trails Manual-CoT on arithmetic average and on commonsense tasks, while exceeding it on Last Letters (pp. 5–6).

The main paper reports text-davinci-003, while text-davinci-002 results are relegated to the appendix (p. 5); the reported evaluation therefore does not establish generalization across model families or scales.

The error analysis uses a random sample of 100 GSM8K problems (p. 7), and the paper describes categorizing error types, so the sample-size concern is grounded. However, it does not say the categorization is subjective, and the claim that this may affect support for the proposed mechanism is an evaluative concern rather than a demonstrated limitation.
